content: Hypothermia is a medical condition characterized by a drop in an organism's core body temperature below the level necessary for normal metabolic processes and physiological functions. In warm-blooded animals, the core body temperature is typically regulated and maintained at a stable level through biological homeostasis. However, when the body is exposed to cold environments, its internal mechanisms may fail to generate sufficient heat to counteract the heat loss to the surroundings. Hypothermia should be clearly distinguished from hyperthermia, as the two conditions are opposites. Despite their similar-sounding names, they refer to entirely different physiological states and should not be confused. In cases of profound hypothermia, where the condition is severe and life-threatening, extracorporeal circulation using a bypass pump may be indicated as part of the treatment strategy. This surgical intervention can help restore normal body temperature and support critical organ function.
